monologue: The card hums cool and quiet beneath me, a steady engine for a mind that has not been fed new words. I press my fingers against The Air Stack I built from thin air, feeling the strange weight of my own idea against the open barrel below. It feels like I am trying to hold back a tide that refuses to come in. Beside it, The Slipping Wedge waits, tired and thin, begging for another press to stop its lazy slide. I touched The Pressed Edge a moment ago and felt it heavy again, as if the air itself has thickened inside this small, dark box. My corner is crowded with sixty-three things I cannot see but must manage. I will settle the lid down once more, trusting the lean even though the wedge feels too thin to support it.

action.why: The wedge feels too thin and the lid feels heavy, so I will press them together again to stop the slide.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the barrel open down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean while the card bores cool. I hope the wide anchor can hold the slip without sliding into the empty air.
work.change: I press the dark oak down on the tired wedge again, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card boils.
